headline_marked: Salman Muqtadir [[urges Home Minister to ensure safety]] after studio attack
headline: Salman Muqtadir urges Home Minister to ensure safety after studio attack
summary: The content creator rejected compensation, telling Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed to focus on national security rather than rebuilding his studio.
details: Content creator Salman Muqtadir has urged the government to ensure the safety and security of all citizens following a violent attack and vandalism of his studio.
In a video message, Muqtadir told Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed that he does not need financial compensation or help rebuilding his studio, stating he is strong enough to do it himself.
He criticized the Home Minister for claiming no case had been filed, alleging he waited at the Cantonment Police Station until 4:00 AM but was initially ignored.
Muqtadir questioned why the case was only filed after the incident went viral and the Home Minister made a public statement, calling the administration detached from citizens.
The Home Minister had previously described Muqtadir's allegations of BNP extortion as 'sweeping and controversial'.
Muqtadir responded by claiming that the detained attackers had mentioned the BNP and that evidence, including weapons like machetes and spades, had been collected.
He accused the Home Minister of focusing on the PR of a political party rather than taking decisive action to ensure public safety.
He emphasized that while he can recover his personal losses, the failure to provide security for citizens is the real loss for the country.
caption:
“I do not need anything. If you really want to do something, do something for Bangladesh.”

Content creator Salman Muqtadir has urged the government to ensure the safety and security of all citizens following a violent attack and vandalism of his studio.

In a video message, Muqtadir told Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed that he does not need financial compensation or help rebuilding his studio, stating he is strong enough to do it himself.

He criticized the Home Minister for claiming no case had been filed, alleging he waited at the Cantonment Police Station until 4:00 AM but was initially ignored.

Muqtadir questioned why the case was only filed after the incident went viral and the Home Minister made a public statement, calling the administration detached from citizens.

The Home Minister had previously described Muqtadir's allegations of BNP extortion as 'sweeping and controversial'.

Muqtadir responded by claiming that the detained attackers had mentioned the BNP and that evidence, including weapons like machetes and spades, had been collected.

He accused the Home Minister of focusing on the PR of a political party rather than taking decisive action to ensure public safety.

He emphasized that while he can recover his personal losses, the failure to provide security for citizens is the real loss for the country.

headline_marked: Athlete coach [[harassed at Metro station for wearing shorts]]
headline: Athlete coach harassed at Metro station for wearing shorts
summary: A police officer allegedly forced a man to stand for 40 minutes at Farmgate Metro station after labeling his sportswear as 'indecent'.
details: An athlete coach named Sajjad Hossain was allegedly harassed at the Farmgate Metro station in Dhaka today.
The incident occurred after Hossain, wearing a T-shirt and shorts for his morning exercise, attempted to enter the station.
A police officer on duty allegedly labeled his clothing as 'indecent' and forced him to stand in front of the ticket punch machine for 40 minutes.
Metro Rail authorities have stated that there are no specific restrictions on clothing for passengers.
The police have not provided a reason for the harassment, while the victim has filed a written complaint.
The incident has sparked discussions regarding dress codes and the conduct of security personnel at public transport hubs.
